ledger.note: 1258: the Mongols set up Ssangseong Prefecture in Goryeo's north-east. 'In 1258, Yuan dynasty general San Gil and Bo Ji invaded northeastern Goryeo along with the eastern Jurchen. They then surrendered the land north of Cheollyeong Pass to Yuan dynasty.' The Mongol invasions page has only 'who established Ssangsong Prefecture in their area', with 1258 inferred from the context of the winter of 1258. The Yuan dynasty did not yet exist (Cliopatria's Mongol Empire row runs 1206..1293); the page's wording is used.

ledger.note: 1356: Goryeo takes Ssangseong back. 'attacked Yuan dynasty together with Dongnyeong Prefectures and restored the land' and 'Ssangsŏng prefecture fell to Goryeo in 1356'; Yu Inu was sent by King Gongmin to take it. The goryeo dossier carries the matching gain.

notes: Colony (Mongol outpost) on Goryeo land, 98 years. Overlord: the Mongol Empire (Cliopatria 1206..1293) then the Yuan dynasty (1294..1374); the pages do not date the change of label. Rulers: the General Superintendents were the Cho family (Cho Hwi, his son Cho Yanggi, grandson Cho Rim, great-grandson Cho Sosaeng) and the chiliarch post passed to the T'ak family; no reign years on the page, so no strip. The page does not mention the Yi family of Yi Seong-gye, which a reader may expect. Goryeo's own claim to the area in these years (as a vassal of the Yuan from about 1259-1270) is the goryeo dossier's. The Mongol invasions page dates the prefecture only by context.
